HYPERKALAEMIA = K+ > 5.5mmol/l 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
MANAGEMENT  
 
* Stop exogenous K+ administration 
* Stabilise the cardiac membrane (see table) 
* Shift K+ intracellularly & increase K+excretion (see table) 
* Treat the underlying cause 
* Follow-up monitoring of potassium

CAUSES 
 
*Impaired excretion 
  e.g. renal failure, drugs (spironolactone),  
          hypoaldosteronism (Addison’s) 
*Transcellular shifts 
   e.g. haemolysis (2 rhabdomyolysis), acidosis,  
          hyperglycaemia 
*Measurement error 
   e.g. haemolysis during phlebotomy 
STABILISATION & K+ SHIFTING & EXCRETION 
ECG CHANGES 
* Tall, peaked T-waves 
* Prolonged PR interval 
* Widened QRS 
* Flattening/broadening/loss of P waves 
* Sine wave (S & T waves merge) 
* Arrrythmias 
* Cardiac arrest à PEA/VF/VT/asystole
